$comment: Lane declarations. A lane is the whole difference between one build target
and another, expressed as data so that adding a third lane is a row here
rather than a new script. run-build.sh and run-build-1vivy.sh differed only
in tree and status file, and choosing wrongly between them was itself a
governed_manifest is the local manifest that declares which projects this
lane owns. Those projects, plus the build-patch overlay targets, are the set
the identity is folded over; everything else in the tree is pinned by

reconciliation.mode says how a lane reaches the published state. published-head: the tree syncs directly to the published commits, so HEAD must equal them. replayed-profile: the tree syncs to a base and replays the published patch series locally, which RE-AUTHORS every commit - so HEAD can never equal the published commit and comparing them reports a correct tree as broken. Those projects are judged on HEAD^{tree} against series.json head_tree_sha, which is exactly why series.json records both.

1vivy.description: the 1vivy consumer tree, synced from published repos only
